2027-06-16.title: Wednesday of the Eleventh Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Blessed the man who fears the Lord
Your Father who sees in secret will reward you
2027-06-16.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 11 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-06-16.verse: Each of you must give as you have made up your mind, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
theo: St Paul is still speaking about the collection for the poor of Jerusalem, and now he uses the language every farmer understands: “The point is this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.” A farmer who keeps back most of his seed for fear of losing it will have a poor harvest. Giving to the poor is not throwing seed away; it is sowing. Then Paul adds a word about the heart of the giver: “Each of you must give as you have made up your mind, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.” The Greek word for cheerful is hilaros, from which comes our word “hilarious.” God does not want gifts squeezed out of us by guilt or by public pressure; he wants the gift of a glad heart. And the one who gives in this way will never be the poorer: “God is able to provide you with every blessing in abundance, so that by always having enough of everything, you may share abundantly in every good work.” Paul quotes today's Psalm about the just man: “He scatters abroad, he gives to the poor; his righteousness endures forever.” God, “who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food,” will multiply our seed. And the final fruit of all giving is not only bread for the poor but praise for God: our generosity “will produce thanksgiving to God.”

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of the three great works of Jewish piety, which the Church still practises: almsgiving, prayer and fasting. He does not question these practices; he takes for granted that his disciples will give, pray and fast. He asks only one question: for whom are you doing it? “Beware of practicing your piety before others in order to be seen by them; for then you have no reward from your Father in heaven.” The word “hypocrite” in Greek meant a stage actor, someone playing a part behind a mask. Jesus describes the actor's way: sounding a trumpet when giving alms, praying “at the street corners, so that they may be seen by others,” disfiguring the face while fasting. Three times he says: “Truly I tell you, they have received their reward.” They wanted applause, and they got it, and that is all they will get. Then three times he describes the way of the child of God: “do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing”; “go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret”; “put oil on your head and wash your face.” And three times comes the same promise: “your Father who sees in secret will reward you.” This does not forbid public worship or good example; a few verses earlier Jesus said, “let your light shine before others” (Matthew 5:16). The difference is the direction of the heart: the light is to give glory to the Father, not to ourselves.
outline: Ask: if no one ever knew about my good deeds, would I still do them?
Giving is sowing; God multiplies the seed of the generous.
God wants the gift of a glad heart, not of reluctance or pressure.
Alms, prayer and fasting done for the Father who sees in secret.
“Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
live: Decide today, in your heart, a gift for someone in need, and give it gladly, without waiting to be asked.
Find ten minutes today to pray alone, in a quiet room with the door shut, to your Father who sees in secret.
2027-06-16.prayer: Generous Father, you supply seed to the sower and bread for food, and you love a cheerful giver. Release our hearts from fear and meanness, so that we may sow bountifully and share abundantly in every good work. Lord Jesus, you saw the hypocrisy of those who wanted to be seen; purify our alms, our prayer and our fasting, so that we may do them for the Father who sees in secret, and our generosity may produce thanksgiving to God. Amen.
altar: At every Mass the gifts of bread and wine are brought to the altar, and with them the collection for the needs of the Church and the poor. The Eucharist is the perfect gift: Christ offering himself to the Father, not to be seen by others, but in the hidden obedience of love. United with his sacrifice, our small gifts become a thanksgiving to God.

quick: Paul: whoever sows bountifully will reap bountifully; give as you have decided in your heart, for God loves a cheerful giver.
God gives abundantly to the generous, so that they may share in every good work, and their giving becomes thanksgiving to God.
Jesus: give alms, pray and fast not to be seen by others but in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
2027-06-16.action: Do one good deed today that no one will ever know about, except your Father in heaven.
2027-06-16.question: For whom do I really give, pray and fast: for God, or for the eyes of others?

family.explain: Jesus says: when you do something good, do not show off. When you share, do it quietly. When you pray, you can go into your room, close the door and talk to God alone. God sees everything, even the things nobody else sees, and he is happy with what we do for him with love.
family.intention: We pray for the poor in our neighbourhood, and for all who help them quietly.
family.ask: Ask: “What secret good deed can each of us do for someone in the family this week?” Then do it without telling!

illus: For many years the poor families of a parish in Kollam found, every month, a sack of rice and some money left at the door of the parish office, with a note: for those who need it. Nobody knew who brought it. When an old fisherman of the parish died, his son found in his house a notebook with the dates and amounts carefully written down, every month for twenty-two years. The man had never been rich, and had never spoken of it to anyone, not even to his own family. At his funeral the parish priest read only one line from the Gospel: your Father who sees in secret will reward you. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Father, you love a cheerful giver and you see in secret. Give us generous and humble hearts. Amen.
share: The one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully (2 Corinthians 9:6). Am I sowing sparingly or bountifully in my giving?
God loves a cheerful giver (2 Corinthians 9:7). Do I give with joy, or reluctantly?
Your Father who sees in secret will reward you (Matthew 6:4). What do I do only to be seen?
pm.resp: Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that her works of charity may be done with humility and joy.
For the poor and the hungry, and for all who share their bread in secret.
For those who are tempted to do good only for praise.
For all who pray and fast for others, hidden and unknown.
For our group, that our prayer may be true and our giving cheerful.
pm.close: Father, you see in secret and you reward the hidden gift. Make us cheerful givers and sincere in prayer. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul speaks to us today like a farmer: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully (2 Corinthians 9:6). When we give to the poor, we are not losing; we are sowing. And God is the one who gives the harvest. He supplies seed to the sower and bread for food.

Paul also says: God loves a cheerful giver (2 Corinthians 9:7). Not a giver who is forced, not a giver who complains, not a giver who gives only because his name will be read out in church. God loves the one who gives with a glad heart. Sometimes the poorest give most cheerfully, because they know what it is to be in need.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks about our good works: almsgiving, prayer and fasting. He says: do not do them to be seen by others. The hypocrites wanted to be praised, and Jesus says: they have received their reward (Matthew 6:2). If we give only to get a photograph in the newspaper, or pray only so that others think we are holy, we already have our reward: the praise of people, which lasts a moment.

Instead, Jesus invites us to a secret life with the Father: go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you (Matthew 6:6). Let us today do one good thing that nobody will ever know about. Let us give one gift with a cheerful heart. And let us find one quiet moment to pray behind a shut door. The Father sees, and that is enough. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: when you do something good, you do not have to show everyone. You can do it in secret! Maybe you can make your sister's bed when she is not looking, or put a coin in the box for the poor without telling anyone. Jesus says God sees everything, even secret good deeds, and he is very happy with them. Try one secret good deed today!

intro: Theme: “Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
Giving as sowing, the cheerful heart God loves, and the hidden life of alms, prayer and fasting.

sub: The God who supplies seed to the sower.
q: If you have many possessions, make your gift from them in proportion; if few, do not be afraid to give according to the little you have.
The point is this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
points.apply: Set aside a fixed part of your income this month for the poor, and give it before you spend on yourself.

q: They have given to the poor; their righteousness endures forever;
Each of you must give as you have made up your mind, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
points.apply: Give one gift this week with a smile and without telling anyone.

sub: Alms, prayer and fasting for the Father.
q: O Lord, you have searched me and known me.
But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Choose one hidden practice this week: a secret alms, a quiet prayer behind a shut door, or a small fast offered for someone in need.

concl: Giving is sowing, and God loves the glad heart that gives without reluctance.
Alms, prayer and fasting are done for the Father who sees in secret, not for the applause of others.
2027-06-16.resolve: Do one good deed each day this week that only God will know about.
